title: Preparation of Ex-Vivo Brain Slices for Physiology Experiments
author: Enrico Zampese
materials: Terminally anesthetize the mouse according to institutional protocols.
Move the holding stage into the slicing chamber.

steps.title: Prepare Solutions and Equipment
steps.instruction: Prepare fresh aCSF and slicing solution and begin bubbling them with O2/CO2 gas mixture. A few hours or a day before the procedure, freeze approximately 200ml of slicing solution.

steps.title: Create Slicing Slushie
steps.instruction: Prepare a 0-4 °C slicing solution slushie using an immersion blender to mix pre-frozen slicing solution with freshly-made slicing solution in a large beaker.

steps.title: Set Up Recirculation System
steps.instruction: Establish a recirculation loop for the slushie using a peristaltic pump and tubing with a 27G needle attached to the connector, placing the needle back into the slushie.

steps.title: Prepare Holding Chamber
steps.instruction: Pour aCSF into the holding chamber and place it in a heated water bath at 34 °C under continuous bubbling.

steps.title: Prepare Dissection Area
steps.instruction: Set up two large trays filled with ice.

substeps.instruction: In the first tray, model the ice to create an inclined area for the mouse and pre-chill dissection tools in the remaining ice.
In the second tray, place a petri dish upside-down on the ice and cover it with filter paper; dig a second empty dish into the ice for later use with slicing slushie.

steps.title: Prepare Vibratome Tools
steps.instruction: Lay a precision wipe over ice and place razor blades, a 0.5x0.5in agar block, and the vibratome holding stage on it to keep them cold.

steps.title: Configure Vibratome Settings
steps.instruction: Turn on the vibratome and set the parameters (recommended for striatal coronal slices: 220µm thickness, 0.06 mm/s speed, and 1mm oscillation amplitude).

steps.title: Perform Vibration Check
steps.instruction: Insert the double-edge blade into the holder and use the vibro-check tool to minimize vibration, then remove the vibro-check apparatus while leaving the blade in.

steps.title: Prepare Slicing Chamber
steps.instruction: Place the vibratome slicing chamber in the vibratome ice tray and fill the surrounding area of the tray with ice.

steps.title: Verify Anesthesia
steps.instruction: Bring the anesthetized mouse to the dissection area and verify full anesthesia by pinching a posterior paw to check for the absence of a pain reflex.

steps.title: Position the Mouse
steps.instruction: Secure the mouse in a supine position with the head oriented away from the operator (or facing downward if the area is inclined).

steps.title: Expose the Thoracic Cavity
steps.instruction: Expose the peritoneal cavity and rib cage by cutting the skin just below the sternum and cutting the fascia connecting the skin to the rib cage.

steps.title: Expose the Heart
steps.instruction: Carefully cut the diaphragm without damaging the beating heart, cut the chest cage, and lift it toward the head (a needle may be used to hold it in position).

steps.title: Perform Transcardiac Perfusion
steps.instruction: Perfuse the mouse with the circulating slicing solution slushie.

substeps.instruction: Insert the needle connected to the peristaltic pump into the left ventricle of the heart.
Rapidly pinch the right atrium with spring scissors to allow dark-red blood to flow out.
Maintain the needle position while the solution washes out the blood (heart should still be beating); use a wash water bottle to remove excess blood if needed.
Continue until the liver looks paler (typically within 10-20s) and blood flow from the right atrium decreases.

steps.title: Extract the Brain
steps.instruction: Remove the brain while maintaining cold temperatures.

substeps.instruction: Remove the perfusion needle and quickly decapitate the mouse with scissors.
Transfer the head into the empty petri dish on ice and submerge it in slicing slushie.
Cut the skin to expose the median line of the skull and remove the posterior part of the skull.
Cut along the median line toward the rostral part; past bregma, make two diagonal cuts toward the eyes and two lateral cuts along the lambdoidal sutures, keeping the head in slushie.
Open the skull with tweezers and gently remove the brain using a spatula, sliding it into the slicing slushie in the petri dish.

steps.title: Mount the Brain
steps.instruction: Prepare and mount the brain onto the vibratome stage.

substeps.instruction: Wet the filter paper on the upside-down petri dish with slicing slushie.
Wipe the vibratome holding stage dry and apply super glue to the center.
Move the brain from the slushie to the filter paper and use a single-edge blade to optimize the orientation for slicing.
Use a spatula to move the brain from the filter paper onto the glue on the holding stage, ensuring the brain and agarose block are properly set.

steps.title: Slicing Procedure
steps.instruction: Slice the brain using the vibratome.

substeps.instruction: Quickly pour slicing slushie into the chamber to cover the brain, set the chamber on the vibratome, and add a small bubbler.
Use a spatula to move residual ice toward the operator to leave the brain visible.
Lower the blade into the solution, adjust position/inclination, set the slicing cycle start/end points, and manually lower the blade near the starting region.
Discard brain fragments and slices from undesired areas until the region of interest is reached.

steps.title: Collect and Recover Slices
steps.instruction: Collect the target slices and allow them to recover.

substeps.instruction: Immediately transfer slices containing the region of interest into the holding chamber at 34 °C.
Allow slices to recover at 34 °C for 30 minutes under constant bubbling.
Remove the holding chamber from the water bath and let slices equilibrate at room temperature for at least 15 minutes before experiments.

steps.title: Cleanup and Disposal
steps.instruction: Clean the workspace and dispose of biological materials.

substeps.instruction: Discard remaining tissue and wash the apparatus and tools.
Collect a tail fragment in an eppendorf tube if genotyping is required.
Discard the mouse carcass and extra tissue in the designated bag.
Dispose of all sharps according to institutional guidelines.
